doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07329.title: Nonlinear Ozone-Phytoplankton-Sea-Ice Coupling Regulates Fine-Scale Gaseous Elemental Mercury Enhancement in the Arctic Marginal Ice Zone
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07329.summary: Abstract Arctic marginal ice zone (MIZ) is a key summertime source of elevated atmospheric gaseous elemental mercury (GEM), but controls on its spatial variability remain unclear. Multiscale spatial statistics, machine learning, and quantile regression were applied to MOSAiC in situ observations (June-September 2020). GEM exhibits strong fine-scale spatial autocorrelation at 10 km (Moran’s I = 0.876). Random forest model (R2 = 0.85) with SHAP attribution identified ozone (O3), chlorophyll a (Chla), and open water fraction (OWF) as dominant GEM predictors. Quantile regression revealed that nonlinear coupling among OWF, Chla, and O3 strengthens under high GEM concentrations. By further combining spatial analysis with quantile regression modeling, a GEM-sensitive region was identified (OWF = 0.156–0.404, Chla = 1.17–1.57 μg/L, O3 = 9.2–19.7 ppb); within this region, both the O3 × Chla and O3 × OWF interactions exhibited significant positive correlations. The positive effect of O3 × Chla persists across all regions, while the O3 × OWF coupling varies dynamically with the retreat of sea ice. O3 indirectly favors GEM accumulation via regulating phytoplankton, and sea-ice melt exerts stage-dependent modulation of atmospheric oxidizing capacity. This study identifies O3 as a critical MIZ mercury regulator, and embedding O3-mediated pathways in models improves GEM projections under Arctic warming.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c00902.title: Novel Multi-Isotope Am and Cm Signatures Trace Temporal Changes in Nuclear Inputs in a Baltic Sediment Core
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c00902.summary: Abstract Anthropogenic radionuclides have been present in the environment since 1945 due to civil and military uses of nuclear energy. This study represents an extensive characterization of Am and Cm isotopes (241Am, 242mAm, 243Am, 244Cm, 245Cm, 246Cm), and 237Np, in a Baltic Sea sediment core directly impacted by discharges from the Studsvik nuclear research facility (Sweden). Distinct isotopic signatures were identified throughout the sediment core, enabling discrimination between inputs from atmospheric nuclear weapons testing (1952–1965), Sweden’s nuclear-weapons-related activities during the 1970s, and subsequent releases associated with civil nuclear-energy development. The findings demonstrate that higher actinides provide powerful isotopic fingerprints for resolving complex nuclear contamination histories and attributing release sources in environmental archives. This study further establishes the utility of actinide isotopic tracers beyond U and Pu and presents the first environmental application of the 243Am/241Am ratio in a system with well-constrained inputs from distinct nuclear sources.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12044.title: Dipole Polarization Engineering Enables Ultrahigh One-Step Hydroxyl Radical Generation for Low-Chemical Water Decontamination
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12044.summary: Abstract Hydroxyl radicals (•OH) were key radicals for the removal of organic contaminants from water. Peroxymonosulfate (PMS) activation had attracted broad interest as a route to •OH generation because of its asymmetric O–O bonds and ease of storage and transport. However, conventional Fenton-like activation of PMS typically produced •OH through a two-step pathway involving sulfate radicals (SO4•–), which incurred kinetic losses and limited •OH availability. Here, we reported a one-step •OH generation pathway from PMS enabled by synergistic polarization effects. This electronic regulation increased the O–O bond dipole moment from 0.45 to 3.86 D and produced a steady-state •OH concentration more than 2 orders of magnitude higher than those reported for representative state-of-the-art Fenton-like systems. Mechanistic analyses revealed that the amplified dipole promoted heterolytic O–O bond cleavage, thereby bypassing the SO4•– intermediate and enabling direct •OH generation. This system achieved efficient removal of diverse organic pollutants and increased rate constant of oxidant activation by 175–400% higher than the values reported for representative PMS/PDS-based Fenton-like systems. Life cycle assessment further revealed a lower environmental footprint, attributed to improved chemical utilization rates. This oxidant-centered strategy provided a promising route to utilize dipole polarization for efficient generation of •OH, with the potential to achieve scalable and low-carbon advanced oxidation water remediation.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09890.title: A Supervised and Visualization-Enabled Toolkit for Robust DNA Reference Database Construction in eDNA Biomonitoring
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09890.summary: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) and DNA-based technologies are increasingly used for biodiversity assessment, but their taxonomic resolution depends strongly on the quality, completeness, and interoperability of reference databases. Public barcode repositories often contain heterogeneous sequence lengths, inconsistent taxonomy, redundant records, and incomplete metadata, and existing tools do not always provide supervised curation, visual inspection, controlled database extension, and multiformat export in one workflow. Here, we present MFRefData (Multi-Format Reference Database), a Python-based toolkit for constructing customized reference databases using a paired CSV–FASTA architecture. MFRefData integrates NCBI sequence retrieval, primer-specific in silico PCR, standardized taxonomic annotation, VSEARCH-based dereplication, rule-based filtering, controlled database extension, visualization, and export to multiple commonly used compatible formats. Using the Pearl River fishes under standardized input conditions, MFRefData retrieved more sequences and covered more species than the refdb and CRABS toolkits, while also achieving higher sequence retrieval efficiency and memory efficiency. In an in silico mock community of 40 fish species and three mitochondrial 12S primer sets, MFRefData produced more correct species-level assignments than databases generated by the refdb and CRABS toolkits. Applied to real eDNA samples, MFRefData recovered broader species-level biodiversity signals. Overall, MFRefData provides a supervised, visualization-enabled, and multiformat framework for improving reference database transparency, technical quality control, and reproducibility, while supporting more reliable species-level taxonomic assignments in DNA-based biodiversity assessment.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02393.title: Enhanced CO2 Storage Capacity and Hydrate Formation Kinetics Using SDS-Stabilized CO2 Emulsions for Submarine Carbon Hydrate Storage
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02393.summary: Abstract Surfactant-assisted CO2 emulsion injection into cold aquifers offers enhanced CO2 storage capacity and accelerated hydrate formation. However, prior studies have largely treated surfactants as either emulsion stabilizers or hydrate kinetic promoters in isolation, leaving unresolved whether the concentration that optimizes CO2 trapping is compatible with that needed for hydrate formation near submarine temperatures. This study addresses that gap through a systematic, multiscale evaluation of SDS-stabilized CO2 emulsions. At ∼3 °C, SDS precipitates before reaching its critical micelle concentration; solubility, interfacial tension, and bulk hydrate formation experiments identify 1000 ppm as a practical upper limit for porous-medium experiments. High-pressure, low-temperature microfluidic experiments show that SDS above 500 ppm improves CO2–water displacement efficiency by increasing effective CO2-phase viscosity and reducing interfacial tension, yielding smaller CO2 ganglia and stable, piston-like displacement. SDS up to 1000 ppm shortens induction times and increases hydrate film growth rates, following a power-law dependence on subcooling with an exponent of 2. CO2 emulsions further sustain open transport pathways via continued CO2 dissolution, enabling efficient long-term CO2-to-hydrate conversion. These results define a concentration window where SDS simultaneously enhances CO2 storage and hydrate kinetics.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c06286.title: Patterns and Mitigation of Large Language Models’ Hallucinations on Environmental Regulatory Facts
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c06286.summary: Abstract With increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in the environmental education, research, and policy domains, reducing hallucinations─where LLMs confidently produce wrong or fabricated results─remains a critical challenge toward trustworthy agentic AI. We evaluated hallucinations on 505 environmental water, air, and solids regulatory facts collected from U.S., China, the European Union (EU), and the World Health Organization (WHO). Across four open-weight and three commercial state-of-the-art LLMs evaluated in both English and Chinese, open-weight models hallucinated on 50–70% of facts, while commercial models hallucinated on only 7–15%. We discovered a deep geographic and linguistic imbalance, where LLMs hallucinate much less on U.S. facts, and when prompting in English. Although models were less confident on average when hallucinating, a non-trivial fraction of incorrect answers were still produced with high token-level confidence. Causal tracing identified layers where restoring the subject representation most strongly recovered correct answers, with patterns differing across models. Retrieval-augmented generation effectively mitigated hallucination, even for small open-weight models. Safe deployment of AI in high-stakes environmental workflows therefore requires both targeted mitigation of training biases and robust external knowledge grounding.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02171.title: Dual Valorization of Mine Tailings for Critical Metal Extraction and Carbon Capture via Organic Acids
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02171.summary: Abstract The growing demand for critical elements (CEs) and carbon removal solutions creates opportunities to valorize mine waste. We investigate the organic acid-enhanced extraction of critical elements from wollastonite-rich tailings while assessing carbon dioxide (CO2) mineralization potential. Tailings were obtained from a mine in New York and contained aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, manganese, and titanium in wollastonite, pyroxene, garnet, and feldspar phases. Flow-through dissolution experiments at 40 and 80 °C using citric, formic, and oxalic acids (0.001–0.1 M), coupled with online pH, temperature, and pressure monitoring, were conducted, and the data were used to validate a multimineral kinetic model based on population balance equations, aqueous geochemistry, and ligand-dependent dissolution rate laws. Formic and oxalic acids achieved superior extraction, with formic acid particularly efficient for calcium─enabling coupled CEs recovery and CO2 mineralization. The ligand-promoted rate laws show a kinetic order of 0.5–1 with respect to formate activity for all minerals. Moreover, comparison of the estimated rates with previous works shows up to 1 order of magnitude faster dissolution in the presence of 0.1 M formic acid, reaching a plateau around pH 4 as the formate activity becomes constant. Overall, our multimineral kinetic framework demonstrates that model complexity should match element distribution, with mineral-specific kinetic models required for elements concentrated in distinct phases. In this way, the proposed approach provides a predictive tool to support sustainable tailings valorization.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11907.title: Far-UVC Activation of Performic Acid Enables Concurrent Oxidative and Reductive Micropollutant Abatement
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11907.summary: Abstract Conventional UV-driven advanced oxidation and reduction processes generally emphasize one redox regime and can be inhibited by wastewater constituents. Here, we characterize the photochemistry of performic acid (PFA) under 222 and 254 nm irradiation and evaluate the capacity of PFA solution, prepared from H2O2 and formic acid and thus containing residual H2O2 and formate, to generate concurrent oxidative and reductive pathways. Relative to 254 nm, 222 nm irradiation increased the fluence-normalized photodecay rate constants of neutral PFA (PFA0) and its conjugate base (PFA–) by 1.21- and 3.81-fold, respectively. The increase arose from 16.1- and 10.1-fold larger molar absorption coefficients at 222 nm, despite lower fitted innate quantum yields (0.367 and 0.804 molecule photon–1 at 222 nm versus 0.587 and 0.819 molecule photon–1 at 254 nm). The UV222/PFA solution system generated the reductant •CO2– together with oxidative HO• and oxygen-centered organic radicals. Pathway analysis attributed 34% of carbamazepine removal to •CO2– and 19% of naproxen removal to R-O• at 222 nm. Chloride and bromide enhanced fluence-normalized degradation through reactive-halogen chemistry; the largest increases were observed for carbamazepine (47.5-fold at 254 nm and 21.9-fold at 222 nm). In real municipal wastewater, UV222/PFA solution decreased total organic carbon by 33.5% within 60 min, compared with 21.6% under UV254/PFA solution, at an initial PFA concentration of 80 μM. These results suggest far-UVC activation of PFA solution as a dual-redox treatment platform, with the observed advantages maintained in the tested wastewater effluents.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12956.title: Ionizing Radiation Sustains Fenton Oxidation through Radiolytic Fe Redox Cycling for Deep Mineralization of Refractory Pollutants
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12956.summary: Abstract The limited regeneration of Fe(II) from Fe(III) constrains sustained oxidation and mineralization in conventional Fenton processes. Here, we investigate an ionizing radiation-assisted Fenton process (IRFP) in which radiolytic Fe redox cycling sustains Fe-mediated oxidation. Using sulfasalazine as a model pollutant, we demonstrate that radiolytically generated hydrated electrons support two coupled pathways: rapid H2O2 activation and the conversion of Fe(III) to Fe(II). The resulting Fe redox cycling dynamically replenishes the Fe(II) pool alongside radiolytic H2O2 activation, thereby sustaining oxidative transformation beyond the initial degradation stage. Compared with irradiation and conventional Fenton treatment, IRFP promoted deeper fragmentation of azo, sulfonamide, and aromatic structures, resulting in enhanced mineralization. Transformation-product analysis further showed that continued transformation in IRFP reduced the persistence of complex intermediates with elevated predicted toxicity. In real pharmaceutical and coking wastewaters, IRFP achieved effective treatment under near-neutral conditions with substantially lower H2O2 and Fe(II) requirements than Fenton treatment and lower absorbed doses than irradiation alone. Although its electricity demand remained higher than short-time Fenton treatment, the markedly lower dosage of chemicals reduced the potential iron sludge burden and resulted in lower estimated COD-normalized treatment costs under the investigated conditions. These findings establish radiolytic Fe redox cycling as a strategy for sustaining Fe-mediated oxidation and promoting deeper transformation and mineralization of refractory pollutants.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10710.title: Chemically Stratified Urban Boundary Layer: Seasonally Reversing Vertical Changes in the Underlying Chemistry of Atmospheric Oxidation Capacity
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10710.summary: Abstract The vertical structure of atmospheric oxidation capacity (AOC) and its underlying radical chemistry within the urban boundary layer remains poorly characterized, yet it governs secondary pollutant formation. Here, we combined tower-based vertical observations with process-resolved model simulations in Beijing across winter and summer. We find that AOC generally declined with height in both seasons, but radical concentrations exhibit opposite vertical gradients. Notably, enhanced biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions in summer suppress near-surface OH levels, creating a mid-altitude maximum. However, sharp vertical NO gradients drove an increase in ROx with height in winter. The underlying chemistry of vertical AOC variation shifts with the seasons. In winter, the photolysis of HONO dominates ROx production, and NOx-driven ROx loss prevails. In summer, the photolysis of oxygenated VOCs takes over, with radical self-reactions as the primary ROx sink. These findings demonstrate that surface observations alone may provide an incomplete representation of the whole boundary-layer chemistry.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c06458.title: Emerging CRISPR Technologies for Environmental Protection: From Genetic Engineering and Biosensing to Environmental Deployment
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c06458.summary: Abstract Since its discovery, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) has revolutionized biomedical science and engineering with its ability to recognize and edit gene sequences with high specificity and precision. Despite the growing interest in using these capabilities to address environmental and sustainability challenges, the broader potential of CRISPR in environmental systems remains unexplored relative to its biomedical applications. Here, we provide a critical perspective on the emerging use of CRISPR for pollution management, ecological conservation, and environmental monitoring. Rather than viewing CRISPR solely as a gene-editing or biosensing technology, we consider both capabilities together to examine how advances in CRISPR engineering can translate into practical environmental solutions. We highlight the fundamental principles behind CRISPR-based editing and sensing and evaluate the challenges that constrain their transition from proof-of-concept experiments to field deployment, including off-target effects, delivery methods, ecological risks, and low sensitivity. Addressing these hurdles requires a multifaceted approach that integrates emerging technologies such as reversible CRISPR technology, amplification and cascade reactions, and machine learning, with strict regulatory oversight and rigorous risk assessments. This perspective identifies critical strengths, weaknesses, and research priorities for advancing CRISPR from laboratory technology toward robust tools for environmental applications.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09040.title: Microplastics Rapidly Sink and Beach in a Whole-Lake Experiment
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09040.summary: Abstract Although advances in oceanographic and limnological modeling have increased our understanding of microplastic transport and persistence, we require more knowledge to effectively protect biodiversity. We initiated a whole-lake experiment (the pELAstic project) to measure the real-world fate and transport of microplastics. We added microplastics to a boreal lake, simulating stormwater input, at loading concentrations predicted to achieve environmentally relevant concentrations. Here, we introduce our experiment and describe the particle budget from the first microplastic addition. We observed rapid transport of microplastics to different ecosystem compartments. Transport patterns could not be fully explained by initial particle size and density, highlighting how natural processes modify plastic fate in real-world systems. Microplastic fragments rapidly redistributed─exiting the water column and settling on the bottom and shorelines. A particle budget across the water column, bottom sediments, and beaches accounted for 77% of the polyethylene, 48% polystyrene, and >100% polyethylene terephthalate. “Missing” plastic was likely in the nearshore littoral. Our observations suggest that if we prevent further inputs to aquatic ecosystems, microplastics will quickly disappear from the water column─washing up on shorelines and settling on the bottom. Thus, understanding rates of microplastic deposition and burial is critical to forecast the legacy of microplastic pollution.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07061.title: Basalt Application Alters the Nitrogen Budget of Midwestern U.S. Agricultural Soils through Reduced Nitrous Oxide Fluxes and Increased Nitrogen Leaching
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07061.summary: Abstract Land-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW)─applying ground silicate rock to soils─is being explored for sequestration of CO2 from the atmosphere, with impacts beyond carbon storage. Weathering of basalt releases base cations increasing alkalinity and soil pH, which we hypothesized would reduce N2O emissions. Repeated applications of basalt to a heavily fertilized annual Zea mays and Glycine max rotation (maize and soybean) and the low-fertilized perennial bioenergy grass Miscanthus x giganteus (miscanthus) in Illinois raised soil pH from 6.6 to 7.1 in maize/soybean and from 5.4 to 6.3 in miscanthus and consistently reduced annual N2O emissions by 16–40% over 7 growing seasons. Although not statistically significant for any given crop, our results indicate an emerging trend of increased N leaching (23% pooled across crops and years), suggesting a potential shift in N loss from the atmosphere to groundwater. Crop yields increased or remained unchanged, indicating enhanced weathering is compatible with conventional farming practices. Regional land model simulations show that ERW deployment across the US Corn Belt could reduce soil N2O emissions by 11% under a moderate deployment pathway and by 24% under a more intensive deployment pathway. The effects of enhanced weathering extend beyond CO2 sequestration and may benefit both greenhouse gas mitigation and bioenergy crop production, with a potential trade-off of increased N mobility in fertile, organic matter-rich US Midwestern soils.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10645.title: Biomass Hydrothermal Reduction Enables Direct Copper Recovery from Wastewater
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10645.summary: Abstract Recovering copper (Cu) from strongly acidic copper wastewater (SACW) is essential for resource sustainability and environmental preservation, but conventional technologies bear high economic costs and generate secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate a biomass waste-mediated hydrothermal reduction process that simultaneously removes and recovers Cu as metallic Cu from SACW. The process operates under mild conditions (180 °C, 7 h) and achieves over 99% removal of Cu(II) across a wide concentration range, directly reducing Cu(II) to metallic Cu(0) without incorporation into hydrochar. Notably, the liquid products from biomass hydrothermal treatment, particularly 2-furoic acid, served as electron donors for Cu(II) reduction, with its C2/C3 atoms potentially providing electron transfer channels that drive the stepwise reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). In a 5 L pilot test with two types of industrial wastewater, the technology achieved >99% Cu(II) removal (residual <0.5 mg/L) and recovered metallic Cu with a purity of 99.9% after simple calcination. Life-cycle assessment and technoeconomic analysis highlight superior economic and environmental benefits when treating high-concentration copper-containing wastewater, establishing a sustainable, generalized hydrothermal reduction platform for efficient Cu recovery from industrial wastewaters. This work establishes a chemistry-driven paradigm for sustainable wastewater treatment, enabling efficient circular recovery of high-value resources from acidic metal-containing wastewaters.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11837.title: Contrasting Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes over the Tibetan Plateau
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11837.summary: Abstract Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m–3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m–3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72–91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09–0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08746.title: Tire-Derived Organic Pollutants across Urban Land Uses: Associations with Traffic Exposure
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08746.summary: Abstract Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and potential drivers in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 compounds exhibited detection frequencies ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-Q ratios and the relative enrichment of N,N′-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD suggest substantial environmental transformation of 6PPD. No statistically significant differences in the concentrations of TDOPs among land-use types or associations with measured soil properties were detected. In contrast, 6PPD exhibited a strong positive association with traffic-derived exposure metrics. The maximum Spearman rank correlation coefficient was observed for the commercial traffic exposure metric at a distance-decay parameter of 800 m (ρ = 0.76), and the association remained significant after optimization-adjusted permutation testing (pperm = 0.00030) and false discovery rate correction (q = 0.0048). This study demonstrates the widespread occurrence of TDOPs in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment and identifies modeled traffic exposure as an important correlate of soil 6PPD concentrations.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09870.title: Toward Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09870.summary: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11699.title: Multitechnique Characterization of Dissolved Organic Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11699.summary: Abstract The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure–function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3–5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8–8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity–hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11654.title: Electron Transfer Pathways Stretching from the Extracellular to Intracellular Membrane in Biohybrids Enable Enhanced CO2 Upcycling to Malate
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11654.summary: Abstract Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) empowers one-step conversion of CO2 to long-chain chemicals under mild conditions, enabling sustainable biomanufacturing and achievement of a circular carbon economy. Although the construction of biohybrids has been explored to enhance the inherently low efficiency of MES, whether the binding modes between nanomaterials and microorganisms dictating CO2 conversion efficiency remain elusive. To address this query, we constructed biohybrids with three distinct integration modes (namely, internalization, outer membrane-contact, and transenvelope) between nanomaterials and Shewanella, enabling to proceed CO2-to-malate conversion. Upon MES-driven CO2-to-malate conversion, the transenvelope biohybrid constituted by polydopamine and Shewanella achieved a marked gram-scale malate titer of 19.14 mmol/L, as a result of the distinctive transenvelope capacity of polydopamine stretching from the extracellular to the intracellular membrane. This transenvelope capacity imparts extended electron transfer pathways spanning from the cytoplasmic membrane to the extracellular space, significantly reducing interfacial barriers at the electrode-microorganism interface and greatly promoting NADH and ATP synthesis for malate synthesis, which can enhance NADH synthesis. This work proposes the construction of a transenvelope biohybrid to optimize microbial metabolism, offering an alternative for the efficient valorization of CO2 to carbon-negative long-chain chemicals.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05063.title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s Carbon Storage Potential
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05063.summary: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c13419.title: Unraveling the Effects of Early Life Air Pollution and Temperature Exposure on Children Being Overweight and Obese: Evidence and Intervention

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10253.title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10253.summary: Abstract Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11569.title: Engineering High-Entropy Interfaces in a Single-Metal Cu System to Drive Concerted Nonradical Catalysis and Pollutant Sequestration
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11569.summary: Abstract Nonradical direct electron transfer (DET) can make advanced oxidation less vulnerable to radical scavenging in complex waters, but requires catalysts with efficient charge transport, stability, and practical synthesis. High-entropy materials provide diverse local environments, yet their multimetal compositions and prolonged heat treatment limit implementation. We combined chemically induced self-internal heating (SIH) with chloride-induced interfacial reconstruction to prepare a single-metal Cu system with high-density grain boundaries (SM-HDGB). SIH formed a Cu-carbon precursor in 3.5 s through an internal pulse above 1200 °C. HCl treatment generated intergrown Cu, Cu2O, CuCl, and Cu2Cl(OH)3 domains spaced 2–10 nm apart, creating phase, oxidation-state, and coordination diversity described as empirical interfacial chemical-state entropy. SM-HDGB completely removed tetracycline within 10 min and increased the apparent rate constant 9.88-fold over the precursor, with little response to 10 mM coexisting anions. Electron paramagnetic resonance, scavenging, filtration, electrochemical, and in situ spectroscopic evidence supported predominantly surface-confined, catalyst-mediated DET. In packed-bed operation, SM-HDGB maintained more than 80% COD removal across four regeneration cycles (approximately 130 h), retained pollutant-derived organic products, and produced near-neutral effluent compatible with Chlorella growth. Laboratory-scale screening estimated at least 96.3% lower synthesis energy demand than conventional routes. Chemical-state-diverse single-metal interfaces can therefore couple rapid peroxydisulfate activation with stable continuous-flow treatment.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09725.title: TP-Agent: An Auditable LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09725.summary: Abstract Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09376.title: Near-Real-Time Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol Optical Depth in China
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09376.summary: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09528.title: Turning Abandoned Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region Goafs under Permafrost Conditions
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09528.summary: Abstract Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10833.title: Aldehyde-philic Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric Environments
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10833.summary: Abstract Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an “aldehyde-philic portal modification” strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal–organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH−π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π–π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an “outer capture–inner fixation” pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07619.title: Global Analysis and Prediction of Bicarbonate in Groundwater under Climate Change
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07619.summary: Abstract Bicarbonate (HCO3–) is a major contributor to the alkalinity of groundwater, and low concentrations can reduce buffering capacity and increase the potential susceptibility of water to corrosion-related quality deterioration, particularly in untreated groundwater systems with corrosion-prone infrastructure. Here, we use machine learning and a comprehensive data set of 28,902 groundwater samples from 80 countries to produce a global probability map of HCO3– concentrations below 80 mg/L and estimate the population residing within the Low-Alkalinity Corrosion Risk Potential Zone (LACRPZ). From 2000 to 2020, LACRPZ was mainly concentrated in Southeast Asia and South America, with approximately 704 million people residing within these zones, particularly in Oceania (52.92%) and South America (35.09%). Although the area of LACRPZ is projected to decline under future climate change, the resident population in LACRPZ is expected to increase. This study reveals the evolution of global groundwater bicarbonate concentrations and resident population, underscoring the importance of integrating bicarbonate into water safety management strategies.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07580.title: Evaluating Pollution Prevention Effectiveness for Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences Methods
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07580.summary: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.5c17288.title: Strategies for Eliminating Heavy Air Pollution in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region: Insights from Joint Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
doi:10.1021/acs.est.5c17288.summary: Abstract The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10806.title: Gradient-Charge Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature CH3CN Emission Control
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10806.summary: Abstract Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c03151.title: A Scenario-Based Probabilistic First-Tier Screening of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c03151.summary: Abstract Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11059.title: Unignorable Role of Iron Redox and Microbial Adaptation in Mediating Arsenic-Induced Suppression of Carbon Emissions in Paddy Soils
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11059.summary: Abstract Arsenic (As) contamination disturbs organic carbon (OC) cycling in paddy soils, potentially influenced by microbial adaptive evolution and redox-active iron (Fe). Here, the association of As with C emissions (CH4 and CO2), microbes, and Fe dynamics in flooded paddy soils was investigated via microcosm experiments across two As levels (20 and 200 mg kg–1). Results showed that As contamination markedly inhibited CH4 (>90%) and CO2 (>38%) emissions, accompanied by inhibited ferric reduction, decreased OC bioavailability, and shifted microbial communities toward As-tolerant and oligotrophic strategies. Correlation analysis and validation experiments demonstrated that Fe reduction covaried negatively with available As but positively with C bioavailability indicators (p < 0.001). The suppressed C emissions under low-dose As were closely linked to perturbed Fe redox cycling, while high-dose As appeared to amplify this inhibition through additional microbial toxicity and community restructuring. Exogenous zerovalent iron increased CH4 emissions by 0.92–19.54-fold through coupled changes in As immobilization, redox conditions, C bioavailability, and abundance of Fe-reducing bacteria and methanogens. This work indicated that Fe redox and microbial adaptation are important contributors to As-mediated suppression of C emissions, providing evidence for the As–Fe–C nexus and offering insights for balancing As remediation with C emission mitigation.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11259.title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory Crosstalk
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11259.summary: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05057.title: Quantitative Fish Biomonitoring by an Enhanced eDNA Metabarcoding Approach
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05057.summary: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA)-based technologies have been increasingly employed in biodiversity surveys and ecological status assessments. However, most eDNA metabarcoding studies rely on relative read abundance, which limits their utility for quantitative environmental management and decision-making. To address this, we developed a quantitative calibration method incorporating dual internal standards: one added prior to DNA extraction and a three-concentration gradient added prior to PCR amplification, enabling independent correction of efficiencies for both steps. Results showed that within the tested aquatic matrices, DNA extraction efficiency had a greater impact on species quantification than PCR amplification efficiency. The dual internal standard calibration outperformed the single internal standard approach in both controlled laboratory experiments and field aquaculture ponds. The spiking of dual internal standards demonstrated excellent calibration across a wide range (2.4–54.1%), indicating that the method is broadly applicable and expandable without altering species detection. Field biomonitoring in the Yangtze River revealed that calibrated eDNA monitoring enhanced the spatial distribution patterns of an endangered species (Leiocassis longirostris) and a migratory species (Coilia nasus). Overall, calibrating DNA extraction and PCR amplification efficiency significantly improves the technical precision of eDNA quantification. While it strongly correlates with biomass under controlled conditions, in field applications, this dual calibration provides a robust analytical baseline that, when combined with ecological models, will be valuable for biodiversity conservation and ecological assessment. Pilot optimization of internal standard spiking volume is recommended for field surveys to balance sequencing cost and quantitative performance.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08458.title: A Substitution Paradox in China’s Plastics Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on Energy-System Decarbonization
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08458.summary: Abstract Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China’s plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c04830.title: Paleoclimatic Legacies Help Explain Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency in Thawing Permafrost
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c04830.summary: Abstract Microbial decomposition in thawing permafrost mobilizes one of Earth’s largest organic carbon reservoirs, releasing CO2 that amplifies global warming. This carbon–climate feedback depends strongly on microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE)─the ratio of biomass carbon synthesis to total carbon uptake, which governs the balance between carbon retention and respiratory loss. Although permafrost carbon and microbial communities developed thousands of years ago, how paleoclimatic legacies shape permafrost CUE remains unresolved. Here, by integrating 18O–H2O labeling with amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across a ∼1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau, we show that mid-Holocene paleoclimate outperforms contemporary drivers in explaining spatial variation in permafrost CUE. Sites with drier and more variable paleoclimates exhibited lower CUE (0.17 ± 0.07) than wetter and more climatically stable sites (0.43 ± 0.08). This lower CUE was linked to two pathways: geochemical constraints involving reduced nutrient availability and stronger phosphorus limitation, and microbial adaptations reflected in communities enriched in metabolically costly stress-tolerance and recalcitrant carbon-acquisition traits. Collectively, these paleoclimatic legacies accounted for 70% of CUE variation, underscoring the critical role of paleoclimate in shaping the vulnerability of permafrost carbon to respiratory loss upon thawing. Incorporating these millennial-scale legacies into Earth system models could improve projections of future permafrost carbon feedbacks.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11443.title: Microplastics Promote Light-Driven Ferrihydrite Transformation by Altering the Balance between Interfacial Aggregation and Redox Processes
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11443.summary: Abstract Ferrihydrite (Fh) phototransformation regulates iron cycling and the mobility of nutrients and contaminants in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Microplastics (MPs) increasingly coexist with Fh, yet whether intact MP particles regulate Fh phototransformation through particle-scale interfacial effects remains unclear. We investigated how MPs (polystyrene (PS), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA)) affect Fh transformation under simulated solar irradiation. Without MPs, irradiation produced predominantly hematite (Hm), with goethite (Gt) as a minor product, and 9.17% of Fh was transformed after 25 d. MPs increased the transformation without changing detectable products. MPs suppressed Fh reaggregation by shifting surface charge and disrupting Fh–Fh contacts, while enhancing irradiation-induced charge separation, surface Fe(III) reduction, Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling, and Fe mobilization. The promoting effects outweighed aggregation inhibition, causing net promotion of Fh transformation. Notably, PLA hydrolysis and photo-oxidation lowered pH and released acidic, Fe-complexing photoproducts, amplifying Fe mobilization and the aqueous Fe pathway. Overall, the PLA > PVC > PS trend reflects coupled polymer chemistry, particle properties, intact-particle interactions, and irradiation susceptibility, with PLA-derived aqueous components providing an additional solution-phase contribution. These findings show that intact MPs and polymer-derived aqueous products jointly modify Fe mineral evolution, linking plastic aging to iron biogeochemistry in illuminated surface environments.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09829.title: Plankton Size Structure Impacts PAH Bioaccumulation and Fate in Marine Pelagic Food Webs
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09829.summary: Abstract Plankton constitutes the primary entry point of contaminants into pelagic food webs, yet the role of plankton size structure in governing hydrocarbon fate remains poorly understood due to methodological limitations. Here, polycyclic aromatic (PAHs) and aliphatic (AHs) hydrocarbons were investigated across seven plankton size fractions (0.7 μm to >500 μm) collected in coastal waters of the northwestern Mediterranean Sea using a locally designed online sequential filtration system. Biochemical, isotopic, and molecular marker analyses were combined to characterize plankton composition, hydrocarbon sources, and PAH bioaccumulation patterns across size fractions. Molecular markers confirmed the transition from phytoplankton-dominated signatures in the smallest fractions to increasing zooplanktonic contributions in larger fractions. The 0.7–2.7 and 2.7–20 μm fractions, dominated by pico- and nanoplankton, accounted for the highest particulate organic carbon and hydrocarbon concentrations (3.0–3.4 μg g–1 dw for Σ26-PAHs) while zooplankton fractions (>60 μm) displayed lower values (0.09–0.69 μg g–1 dw). The passive uptake of low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs dominated across all size fractions but decreased with increasing plankton size. In contrast, high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs showed preferential accumulation in nanoplankton. These results demonstrate that plankton size structure and biomass dependent processes strongly influence PAH bioaccumulation and trophic transfer in marine pelagic food webs.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11406.title: Rapid Emission–Economy Decoupling alongside the Urbanization of Chinese Counties
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11406.summary: Abstract As China makes progress in air pollution control, the growing need for targeted pollution mitigation poses a great challenge for fine-scale emission tracking. However, the lack of up-to-date high-resolution emission data precludes a timely, spatially detailed assessment of emission distributions and their evolution with economic development. Here we derive summertime nitrogen oxides emissions from 2018 to 2024 for a total of 2,842 counties at different levels of urbanization in mainland China, based on satellite measurements and a fast, physics-based emission inversion method. The results show widespread declines in 84.1 ± 7.3% of counties. Among the 1,779 counties with available gross domestic product data, 76.7 ± 7.1% achieve absolute emission-economy decoupling (i.e., reduced emissions despite economic growth), and an additional 9.4 ± 3.9% exhibit relative decoupling (i.e., economic growth outpacing emissions growth). Relative emission reductions and emission-economy decoupling tend to be stronger in more urbanized counties, with the share of total national emissions moving toward less-urbanized, previously less-focused counties, particularly in the west. These results suggest structural progress toward greener development in Chinese counties along with an emerging need to shift attention toward less-urbanized locations.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05738.title: Unresolved Complex Mixture of Hydrocarbons as a Potential Stratigraphic Anthropogenic Marker for the Great Acceleration
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05738.summary: Abstract The unresolved complex mixture (UCM) consists of chromatographically unresolvable branched, cyclic, and aromatic hydrocarbons, which are intermediate- to semivolatile organic compounds primarily derived from anthropogenic fossil fuel usage, including industrial emissions and gasoline and diesel exhaust. The UCM in natural archives, expressed as its ratio to resolved compounds (UCM/R), may thus provide an indication of fossil fuel-derived contamination in the environment over time. To test this hypothesis, accurately dated sediment records from the Black Sea, the Baltic Sea, and the northeastern Germany Tiefer See lake were analyzed for hydrocarbons. Each record presents a similar temporal pattern with a synchronous main increase of UCM/R in the early 1950s and a decrease in the 1990s. This UCM/R pattern most likely reflects the pronounced increase in the use of petroleum-derived products during the Great Acceleration of the mid-20th century and, subsequently, the application of filters and catalytic converters to reduce volatile organic compound emissions in the 1980s–1990s. Therefore, UCM/R in recent sediments represents a stratigraphic anthropogenic marker for the Great Acceleration in European midlatitudes and, if replicated globally, could be a further marker for the beginning of the Anthropocene as a potential geological epoch.

doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02123-w.title: Palaeoclimate constraints narrow uncertainty in future Arctic winter sea ice projections
doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02123-w.summary: Abstract Arctic sea ice decline has been observed across all seasons and is projected to continue in the future. Relative to historical observations, climate models show their largest biases and uncertainties during winter, when ice cover strongly regulates air–sea heat exchange, ocean mixing and atmospheric circulation. Palaeoclimate records offer opportunities to evaluate model performance beyond the historical period, but applications have remained largely qualitative. Here we compile an Arctic-wide database of mid-Holocene (5–7 thousand years ago) biomarkers to assess sea ice simulations of this past warm period. Using a recently developed proxy system model, we present a Bayesian palaeoclimate model weighting scheme that refines the multi-model mean winter sea ice extent through fully quantitative proxy-model comparisons, accounting for model interdependence and non-stationary proxy seasonality. We demonstrate that, by adjusting the contribution of each model to the ensemble mean based on proxy evidence, model weights can eliminate biases and reduce uncertainties by 85%, to the level of interannual variability. Weighted projections using the same climate models indicate that future winter sea ice extent may be nearly 1 million km 2 lower than prior estimates across forthcoming decades and possible emissions scenarios, with broad implications for Arctic ecosystems, mid-latitude weather, and cryosphere stability.

doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02135-6.title: Trade-offs between soil inorganic and organic carbon driven by multiple global environmental changes

doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02107-w.title: Vegetation increasingly controlled by atmospheric dryness rather than soil moisture
doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02107-w.summary: Abstract Terrestrial vegetation regulates global carbon cycling and climate through responses to water availability. Yet, it remains unclear whether soil moisture (SM) or atmospheric dryness (vapour pressure deficit, VPD) dominates vegetation responses and, more critically, how their relative influence changes over time, limiting predictions of ecosystem–climate feedback under warming. Here we analyse satellite-derived vegetation variability over the past four decades using an explainable artificial intelligence framework that disentangles nonlinear hydroclimatic driver contributions. We show SM dominates vegetation variability in most regions. However, VPD influence has strengthened while SM influence has weakened over time. These changes highlight an asymmetric transition with more SM-dominated ecosystems shifting towards increasing VPD control than vice versa. Changes in the mean and variability of SM and VPD drive this transition by altering plant water-stress responses. Continued warming will probably intensify this pattern as rising VPD and more frequent extreme events strengthen atmospheric constraints on vegetation.

doi:10.1038/s41550-026-03004-3.title: A double debris disc around a white dwarf sculpted by two planetary bodies
doi:10.1038/s41550-026-03004-3.summary: Abstract Many planetary systems survive the metamorphosis of their host stars into white dwarfs, as demonstrated by the detection of dusty circumstellar discs around these stellar remnants and chemical signatures of planetary debris in atmospheres of these stars. A small fraction of these circumstellar discs also contain gas, detected in the form of emission lines from various ionic transitions (most commonly the near-infrared Ca II triplet). All of the 21 known gas discs exhibit double-peaked line profiles characteristic of a rotating flat disc. The mechanism behind the generation of gas is still debated, but for at least one system it has been linked with the presence of a surviving planetesimal embedded within the dust disc. Here we report the discovery of WD J132800.85–145019.95, a new gas-disc system that exhibits quadruple-peaked instead of double-peaked line profiles. These emission lines originate from two separate gaseous rings extending from 0.14 R ⊙ to 0.34 R ⊙ and from 0.54 R ⊙ to 1.93 R ⊙ . We propose that this structure results from the presence of two distinct planetary bodies within these discs, ranging in size from a few kilometres to the size of Pluto. The detection this stable double-disc presents a new challenge for the current models of debris disc formation and evolution.

doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01565-8.title: Winter monsoon variability accompanies Xisha SST–North China hydroclimate teleconnection reversal during the Medieval climate anomaly
doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01565-8.summary: Abstract Winter sea surface temperature (SST) in the South China Sea is a precursor of North China hydroclimate, but the relationship’s long-term stability remains uncertain. Using monthly resolved Xisha coral Sr/Ca-SST and three hydroclimate reconstructions analyzed at native temporal resolution, we find that the Medieval Climate Anomaly (MCA, 1149–1205 CE) is the only sampled interval with a cross-proxy-consistent positive relationship. The annually resolved Zheng record remains positive after detrending and autocorrelation correction ( r = 0.476, p adj = 0.043), whereas non-MCA relationships are predominantly negative or near zero. East Asian winter monsoon (EAWM)-related variability is largest during the MCA among the six intervals, yet its association with teleconnection strength is weak ( r = 0.52, p = 0.29), arguing against a universal threshold. Independent central-Pacific coral evidence indicates altered tropical-Pacific variability. Because winter-to-summer SST memory persists, we interpret the MCA reversal as downstream atmospheric reorganization, with EAWM variability as a possible preconditioning factor.

doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01568-5.title: Strengthened relationship between August Laptev Sea ice retreat and September precipitation in Central China since 2005
doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01568-5.summary: Abstract The intensified interannual variability of September rainfall in Central China has led to increasingly frequent and devastating hydrological disasters over the past two decades. This study identifies the accelerated retreat of August Laptev Sea ice since 2005 as a critical, previously unrecognized precursor for September precipitation in Central China. Diagnostics show that post-2005 sea ice retreat and its heightened interannual variance substantially enhance local ice-ocean-atmosphere coupling compared with pre-2005. The resulting surface warming initiates a persistent “warm Siberia–cold North China” thermal dipole, which suppresses the meridional temperature gradient (MTG) over the Mongolian Plateau. This altered thermal gradient modulates transient eddy activity, driving an equatorward shift of the subtropical westerly jet through transient eddy–mean flow interaction, then strengthening the meridional secondary circulation. This configuration facilitates an anomalous anticyclone over the western North Pacific, with anomalous southwesterly flow on its western flank importing moisture across Central China’s southern boundary. Coupled with deep ascending motion, this process drives enhanced September rainfall. These findings underscore the evolving impact of Arctic cryospheric change on mid-latitude climate, providing valuable insights for seasonal forecasting and water resource management.

doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01583-6.title: Traffic and combustion emission controls leave cooking as a dominant local source of primary PM1 in megacities
doi:10.1038/s41612-026-01583-6.summary: Abstract Megacities frequently suffer from poor air quality, with PM 2.5 concentrations routinely exceeding WHO guidelines and elevating the risk of cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Air quality legislation typically targets primary emissions from traffic, a dominant urban source of PM₂.₅. Here, we present direct, chemically resolved quantification of PM₁ emissions from three contrasting megacity neighbourhoods—London, Beijing and Delhi—revealing the magnitude and diversity of urban sources by applying a novel source attribution approach to eddy-covariance flux measurements using aerosol mass spectrometry. In Delhi, traffic and combustion dominate primary PM₁ emissions. In contrast, cooking is the largest source during mealtimes in London and Beijing, contributing up to 83% of midday emissions and 87% in the early evening in London, and up to 61% and 76%, respectively, in Beijing. These findings suggest that air quality legislation in London and Beijing has effectively reduced non-refractory transport and combustion emissions, allowing cooking to emerge as the largest local source of primary non-refractory PM₁. Although cooking is not included in national, European or global emission inventories, recent estimates from the London Atmospheric Emissions Inventory align well with our observations. Together, these results show that the sources dominating primary non-refractory PM₁ emissions differ from those controlling ambient PM 1 mass. Although cooking is now the leading primary source in London and Beijing, further reductions in urban PM₁ will depend on mitigating secondary formation processes.
